classification_categories.power_calc: Formal a priori power calculation (α, β, effect size specified)
classification_categories.effect_size_estimate: Quantitative estimate from pilot/literature, no formal calc
classification_categories.replication_standard: Appeal to field convention or replication of prior study
classification_categories.resource_constraint: Sample size limited by availability, budget, or cohort size
classification_categories.methodology_determined: Sample size inherently defined by measurement technique or study design (stereology, cryo-EM, single-molecule imaging, complete-specimen census); no separate determination step expected
classification_categories.no_justification: n stated but no reasoning provided
classification_categories.na_or_blank: Field empty, N/A, or not applicable
classification_categories.ambiguous: Text present but insufficient to classify

records.title: Genetic switch between unicellularity and multicellularity in marine yeasts
records.sample_size_raw: No predetermined sample size was used for statistical analysis. Sample sizes were chosen to ensure reproducibility of the observed phenotypes, based on preliminary experiments and consistency across replicates. Sample sizes are comparable to those reported in similar studies in the field (Mitchison Field et al., 2019; Goshima, 2022). All sample sizes are provided in the figure legends.

records.title: Insights into DNA repeat expansions among 900,000 biobank participants
records.sample_size_raw: We used genome sequencing data from UK Biobank and All of Us, which were the largest WGS cohorts available to us and provided ample statistical power to identify genetic modifiers of somatic repeat expansion. Our GWAS on somatic expansion of TCF4 included 40,231 UK Biobank participants and 8,217 All of Us participants. Sample sizes for instability analyses of other STRs are reported in Supplementary Data 5. Phenotypic associations of long repeat expansions were computed in a set of 421,364 unrelated individuals of EUR genetic ancestry in UK Biobank.

records.title: Mitochondrial transfer from glia to neurons protects against peripheral neuropathy
records.sample_size_raw: No statistical calculation was used to predetermine sample size for in vitro and in vivo study. In samples for the in vitro experiments, sample sizes of at least n=3 (biologically independent replicates) were sufficient to ensure reproducibility. Sample sizes were determined based on the similar experiments done previously in Professor Ji's laboratory (Donnelly CR, et al. Nature. 2021.).

records.title: Oral 4′-fluorouridine rescues nonhuman primates from advanced Lassa fever
Bidirectional CRISPR screens decode a GLIS3-dependent fibrotic cell circuit
records.sample_size_raw: For mice, the minimal sample size was set the availability of mice for completing the experiment, with each treatment or genotype consisting of at least n=3. Inbred mice were used and sex-matched, allowing for similar variance between experimental group. In vitro cell culture experiments were performed with at least 3 independent biological replicates for each experiment. This is consistent with previous studies and accounts for biological variability between distinct samples from cell lines. Although statistical methods were not used to calculate sample size, we used a minimum of 3 biological replicates.

records.title: A foundation model for continuous glucose monitoring data
records.sample_size_raw: This studies goal was to build a deep learning model using the HPP dataset, thus no prior knowledge on the expected effect sizes exists, or sample size calculation was done. Samples included in this study are of all the participants who met the inclusion criteria detailed in Shilo et al. (2021). The results reported in the manuscript are those that passed the statistical significance threshold.

records.title: Ultra-high-throughput mapping of genetic design space
CFAP20 salvages arrested RNAPII from the path of co-directional replisomes
records.sample_size_raw: No statistical method was used to predetermine sample size. Sample sizes were chosen for the different experimental approaches based on the technical difficulty and throughput of the individual assays, the chosen sample sizes are consistent with previous publications. For imaging experiments, >100 per replicate were measured while for DNA fibers 100-150 fibers were measured per replicate. flow cytometry based assays measured >30.000 cells before gating. for zebrafish larvae experiments 11-36 animals were used, accordingly with previously published data (Chrystal et al 2022, Nature Communications).

records.title: Ligand-specific activation trajectories dictate GPCR signalling in cells
Ageing promotes microglial accumulation of slow-degrading synaptic proteins
records.sample_size_raw: No statistical methods were used for determining sample size. For most studies, sample size = 3 or 4 was selected because pilot studies demonstrated that 3 replicates sufficed for sufficient replication without large variation and/or out of consideration of TMT-plexing limits. Importantly, n = 3 or more permits statistical analyses. For any study with fewer than 3 replicates, it was due to a constraint in terms of mouse availability.

records.title: Environmentally driven immune imprinting protects against allergy
records.sample_size_raw: Sample sizes were chosen to give a minimum of n = 5 across a minimum of two independent experiments.

records.title: Tumour–brain crosstalk restrains cancer immunity via a sensory–sympathetic axis
records.sample_size_raw: The sample sizes used in this paper were selected based on those used in previous publications (Jin et al. Cell 2019). Exact sample sizes are described in each figure legends or Methods.

records.title: Integrated structural dynamics uncover a new B12 photoreceptor activation mode
records.sample_size_raw: The number of collected and indexed images in TR-SFX experiments necessary to obtain statistically meaningful data has been judged according to the CC1/2 value. For all other experiments, the sample size has been determined based on the SNR.
